title: Associated sheaf of a K-flat complex on an affine scheme is K-flat
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $X=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ [def-pc-scheme]. Let $K^\bullet$ be a cochain complex of $A$-modules that is K-flat, i.e. for every acyclic complex $F^\bullet$ of $A$-modules the total tensor complex $\operatorname{Tot}(F^\bullet\otimes_AK^\bullet)$ is acyclic. Let $\widetilde{K^\bullet}$ be the complex of $\mathcal O_X$-modules obtained by applying the associated sheaf $\widetilde{(-)}$ [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections] termwise, with differentials $\widetilde{d^n}$. Then $\widetilde{K^\bullet}$ is a K-flat complex of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-pc-kflat-complex].

proof.text: The tilde-stalk functor and its tensor bifunctor preserve zero morphisms, as checked explicitly in Lean. Restriction of scalars is additive and preserves coproducts. Apply the proved general total-bifunctor comparison to the natural isomorphism of step 1. This gives U(Tot(F tensor_B stalk(tilde K))) ≅ Tot(U(F) tensor_A K) for every stalk-ring complex F.

proof.text: Restriction of scalars preserves and reflects acyclicity. Indeed, in each degree exactness is the elementwise assertion that every element in the kernel of the outgoing differential is in the image of the incoming differential. Restriction leaves both underlying groups and both maps unchanged. The private lemma acyclic_restrictScalars_iff proves this by ShortComplex.moduleCat_exact_iff.

If F is acyclic over the stalk ring, U(F) is acyclic over A by step 3, so hK makes Tot(U(F) tensor_A K) acyclic. Transport exactness degree by degree across the isomorphism of step 2, then reflect acyclicity using step 3. Every stalk of tilde K is therefore K-flat; the reverse implication of the stalk criterion proves isKFlat_tilde.
